executive_summary: APAC expansion carries a friction score of 72/100, driven by three compounding issues: no owner for the legal/compliance review blocking Japan enterprise sales, a payments dependency on a tight 3-month timeline with no fallback plan, and an infrastructure buildout that hasn't been scoped against the certification calendar. The single highest-leverage move is assigning a named owner for the Japan legal review within 48 hours — until compliance requirements are understood, every downstream timeline is fiction.

friction_hotspots.title: No owner assigned for Japan legal and compliance review
friction_hotspots.why_it_creates_drag: Japanese Qualified Invoice System compliance is a prerequisite for enterprise sales, but no one owns the legal review. Without a named owner, this work will continue to be deprioritized while downstream plans assume it will be resolved.
early_warning_signals: Legal review still unscheduled at next check-in
Revised GTM plan assumes compliance without confirming timeline
No legal resource allocated on team capacity plan

evidence.speaker: Kenji Tanaka
evidence.quote: Not yet. We've been focused on the commercial side. Legal review is on the roadmap but hasn't started.

evidence.speaker: Sophie Laurent
evidence.quote: If we get that wrong, our Japanese clients can't claim tax credits on our invoices. That's a deal-breaker for enterprise buyers.

friction_hotspots.recommended_fix: Assign a named owner (likely someone from Legal or Kenji as interim DRI) for the Japan invoicing compliance review by end of week. Set a 2-week deadline for a written assessment of Qualified Invoice System requirements.
friction_hotspots.owner_recommendation: Ravi Patel (to assign), Kenji Tanaka (interim DRI)
friction_hotspots.target_resolution_window: 48 hours to assign owner, 2 weeks for initial assessment

friction_hotspots.title: Payments multi-currency layer on critical path with no slip buffer
friction_hotspots.why_it_creates_drag: The lightweight multi-currency layer is estimated at 3 months, putting payments readiness at July — leaving zero buffer for a Q4 GA. The fallback (USD-only with manual conversion) has already been flagged as a compliance risk, making this a hard dependency with no viable Plan B.
early_warning_signals: Payments team has not committed to the 3-month estimate in writing
No sprint-level breakdown exists for the multi-currency work
Payments team pulled onto other priorities mid-quarter

evidence.speaker: Kenji Tanaka
evidence.quote: They think they can do a lightweight multi-currency layer in three months if we limit to USD, JPY, and SGD only.

evidence.speaker: Ravi Patel
evidence.quote: Three months for the lightweight version — that puts us at July for payments readiness. That's tight for Q4 GA.

friction_hotspots.recommended_fix: Get a written commitment from the payments team lead with a sprint-level breakdown and explicit assumptions. Identify the top 2 slip risks and define trigger points for switching to Singapore-only launch.

friction_hotspots.title: ISMAP certification timeline incompatible with Q4 Japan launch
friction_hotspots.why_it_creates_drag: ISMAP certification is 4-6 months and hasn't started. Without it, Japan is limited to SMB customers, which breaks the revenue model that assumes 30% enterprise mix by month six. The team acknowledged this but deferred the decision, creating a phantom timeline where Japan Q4 remains on slide decks while being technically impossible.
early_warning_signals: Leadership communications still reference Q4 Japan launch
ISMAP process not initiated within 2 weeks
No SMB-only revenue model created as contingency

evidence.speaker: Diana Osei
evidence.quote: At minimum, ISMAP certification for selling to Japanese government and large enterprise. That's a 4-6 month process.

evidence.speaker: Kenji Tanaka
evidence.quote: The revenue model assumes 30% enterprise mix by month six. If we're SMB-only, we'd need to roughly double the customer count to hit the same revenue target.

friction_hotspots.recommended_fix: Formally communicate to leadership that Japan is a Q2 2027 target at earliest. Start ISMAP certification process immediately to avoid further delay. Create an SMB-only contingency revenue model.
friction_hotspots.owner_recommendation: Ravi Patel (leadership communication), Diana Osei (ISMAP kickoff)

friction_hotspots.title: Nomura partnership in limbo with no decision framework for Singapore-first pivot
friction_hotspots.why_it_creates_drag: The team agreed to 'keep the conversation warm' with Nomura but set no concrete next step, owner, or timeline. If Singapore-first becomes the plan, Nomura engagement needs to be explicitly paused or restructured — ambiguity risks either losing the partner or wasting cycles on a deferred market.
early_warning_signals: No Nomura status update at next check-in
Nomura asks for commitment before team is ready
Kenji continues investing time in Japan GTM while Singapore plan is prioritized

evidence.speaker: Kenji Tanaka
evidence.quote: I wouldn't want to lose momentum on that relationship. I'd suggest we keep the conversation warm and formalize when we have a Japan launch date.

friction_hotspots.recommended_fix: Kenji to send Nomura a brief status email within 1 week: acknowledge Singapore-first pivot, set expectation for Japan timeline update by Q3, and propose a quarterly check-in cadence.

critical_path_risks.blocking_dependency: Payments team capacity and 3-month estimate accuracy
critical_path_risks.due_or_trigger: Payments team sprint plan due within 1 week

ambiguities_to_resolve.ambiguity: Can Singapore standalone unit economics justify the expansion without Japan revenue?
ambiguities_to_resolve.why_it_matters: If Singapore alone doesn't pencil out, the board may reject the phased approach and push for a riskier simultaneous launch.
ambiguities_to_resolve.proposed_clarifying_question: What is the minimum viable revenue from Singapore-only in months 1-6 that makes the expansion worth pursuing, and does the current pipeline support it?

ambiguities_to_resolve.ambiguity: Who on the payments team committed to the 3-month lightweight estimate?
ambiguities_to_resolve.why_it_matters: A verbal 'they think they can' from preliminary conversations is not a commitment. Without a named owner on the payments side, the estimate is unreliable.
ambiguities_to_resolve.proposed_clarifying_question: Has the payments team lead formally reviewed and approved the 3-month timeline, and what assumptions does it depend on?

ambiguities_to_resolve.ambiguity: What is the actual infra team capacity for APAC region buildout given current priorities?
ambiguities_to_resolve.why_it_matters: The 8-10 week estimate may not account for competing priorities. If infra is already at capacity, the buildout timeline could double.
ambiguities_to_resolve.proposed_clarifying_question: What is the infra team's current utilization, and would APAC region work require deprioritizing other committed projects?
